output.title: Aerobic Base Run with Flat Neuromuscular Surges
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy running @ Zone 1-2 → 35 min steady continuous aerobic running @ Zone 2 (5:20-5:35/km) → 6 x 15s flat relaxed speed surges @ Zone 4/5 velocity with 60s easy walking/jogging recovery → Cool down 5 min easy jogging @ Zone 1. Overall: An aerobic base session establishing rhythm on flat terrain while introducing brief neuromuscular flat strides. This activates high-threshold motor units without cardiovascular or metabolic fatigue. Reason: Scheduled on the plan opening day to initiate training volume and re-engage neuromuscular turnover without joint strain. Benefit: Expands aerobic capillary density and mitochondrial volume while sharpening stride mechanics and muscular recruitment. Warning: Keep surges relaxed and upright with quick ground contact; do not strain or turn them into all-out maximal sprints.
output.fueling_tip: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Bodyweight Foundation Strength
output.description: Process: Warm up 8 min dynamic mobility and ankle activation → Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squats: 3x8 each leg, 90s rest → Single-Leg Romanian Deadlifts: 3x8 each leg, 90s rest → Step-Downs off 20cm curb: 3x10 each leg, 90s rest → Glute Bridges with 3s isometric hold: 3x12, 60s rest → Side Plank: 3x30s each side, 60s rest → Cool down 5 min static hip flexor and calf stretching. Overall: A foundational bodyweight resistance session focusing on eccentric control, single-leg stability, and pelvic alignment. It builds orthopedic resilience without external gym equipment. Reason: Scheduled early in Base to construct chassis strength and joint integrity before endurance loading escalates. Benefit: Reinforces eccentric quadriceps strength and pelvic stability required to absorb downhill impact and stabilize trail strides. Warning: Maintain strict knee-over-second-toe tracking on all single-leg movements to avoid patellar shear stress.
output.fueling_tip: Hydrate with 500ml water containing 200-400mg sodium; consume a balanced post-workout protein and carbohydrate meal within 45 minutes.

output.title: Aerobic Recovery Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 5 min brisk walking → 35 min continuous easy recovery running strictly in Zone 1 (6:15-6:45/km) → Cool down 5 min gentle walking and leg shaking. Overall: A gentle, fully conversational recovery run kept well below AeT to stimulate active recovery. It flushes metabolic byproducts while accumulating low-stress aerobic volume. Reason: Placed between strength work and the weekend endurance block to promote tissue repair without adding systemic fatigue. Benefit: Enhances microvascular circulation and parasympathetic tone without depleting glycogen stores. Warning: Monitor heart rate strictly; do not drift above 135 bpm regardless of how comfortable the pace feels.
output.fueling_tip: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Base Aerobic Long Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy progression from Zone 1 to Zone 2 → 85 min steady continuous aerobic running @ Zone 2 strictly below AeT (5:35-5:55/km) → Cool down 10 min gentle walking and light mobility. Overall: An aerobic base long run executed on flat terrain to develop metabolic efficiency and fat oxidation capacity. The duration stays safely within weekly proportionality boundaries. Reason: Anchors the weekend endurance stimulus during the Base phase to build fundamental mitochondrial density and musculoskeletal durability. Benefit: Enhances lipid metabolism, spares glycogen stores, and conditions connective tissues to sustained weight-bearing loads. Warning: Maintain a steady, disciplined effort; do not accelerate late in the run if feeling energetic.
output.fueling_tip: 30-60g carbohydrates per hour + 300-500mg sodium/hr with 400-600ml water/hr. Practice consuming fuel in small increments every 20-30 minutes.

output.title: Rest and Mobility
output.description: Process: Rest day with zero structured running → 15 min optional gentle foam rolling and light passive stretching. Overall: A designated complete rest day to facilitate central nervous system recovery and tissue rebuilding. It balances the 5-day training schedule. Reason: Positioned after the weekend long run to restore muscle glycogen and reduce structural micro-trauma. Benefit: Restores hormonal equilibrium and consolidates structural adaptations from the initial training stimulus. Warning: Avoid strenuous recreational activities or extended periods on your feet to ensure true physiological restoration.
output.fueling_tip: Maintain consistent baseline hydration throughout the day; consume nutrient-dense whole foods rich in complex carbohydrates and lean protein.
